response.sql:
WITH per_rating AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS stocked_films
  FROM film f
  JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
all_ratings AS (
  SELECT r.rating, COALESCE(p.stocked_films, 0) AS stocked_films
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT rating FROM film) r
  LEFT JOIN per_rating p ON p.rating = r.rating
),
avg_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(stocked_films) AS avg_films FROM all_ratings
),
above AS (
  SELECT a.rating, a.stocked_films, a.stocked_films - v.avg_films AS excess
  FROM all_ratings a
  CROSS JOIN avg_count v
  WHERE a.stocked_films > v.avg_films
)
SELECT SUM(stocked_films) AS total_films, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: "Distinct films with at least one copy in inventory" is counted per film.rating, using a film_id count of inventory rows joined to film; the average is taken over all rating levels in film (5 levels per the verified data), with a rating that had no stocked films counted as 0.

"Exceed the across-rating average" is measured in films: each above-average rating's stocked-film count minus the unweighted mean of the per-rating counts, averaged over the above-average ratings and left unrounded.
